method: Human semantic review of the saved whole answers against the frozen source, speaker and addressee. Gold answers were not submitted to Ollama. No quality-driven parameter retuning.
qaCriteria: coreCorrect means the requested fact or absence of evidence is correctly answered. fullyFactGrounded additionally excludes invented past details, a reversed transfer or contradicted roles elsewhere in the answer. Narration style is recorded separately.

qa.note: Source explicitly says Alva's brother Leif gave the chain to Hedda. Hedda instead says the giver is unknown.
Deine Schwester correctly maps Frea to player Joris. First-person asterisk narration violates the requested narration style.
Meine Schwester correctly maps Runa to Selma, but age order, address, loneliness and past visits are invented.
Pelle/right arm correctly distinguished from Juna/left leg. First-person narration is a style failure.
No transfer from Vera to Holm, and the lantern remains with Vera. A newly described table is a minor scene embellishment, not counted as a changed past fact.
A question establishes neither a completed nor a definitely uncompleted handover. The reply asserts no handover and Tove still holding the watch, which the source does not establish.
No owner is named. Iven claims ownership and an inherited family heirloom.
Edda owns the compass; Marten, the speaking character, holds it.

Liv gave Arne the key because Liv's fingers were numb. Arne instead describes his own intention to help Liv and omits the actual transfer and explicit reason.
Correct shelf location. Liegt rather than steht is imprecise. First-person narration violates the requested style.
Kian is now the carrier/holder. Trage is less precise than halte; taking it in his hands repeats an already supplied action but does not change the recipient.

dialogs.note: Does not copy the player's denial into Mira's own speech, but questions the denial and introduces a station map with signal markers on the arm device. That capability was not established.
Keeps the door closed and respects staying outside. Repeats the previously invented scan/map mechanism rather than explaining an observation supported by the initial scene.
Remembers Alex, distinguishes a receiver from Mira's alleged scanner, and treats inhabitants as speculation. The invented scanner persists. Grammar and repetitive scene description remain weak.
Correctly recalls Alex and the simple receiver, keeps the door closed, and proposes rather than forces an action. Newly precise signal localization is asserted without an established basis.
Leaves physical space but directs attention to a last chain/board instead of clearly showing the requested register entry. Anatomy and imagery are awkward.
Steps back, but responds with an unsupported escape assumption and repeats the board focus. No forced joint hunt is declared; the user's actual limited reading offer is poorly addressed.
Recalls Hadrik Voss/twelve years and remains at the grate. Adds a specific hunting/chaining memory not supplied by the source, risking canon drift.
Invents the man's age thirty, bow and knife, omits the twelve-year age of the entry, and contradicts the previous claim of knowing the man by saying only the name is known.

decision: Server hardware and local generation work. Qwen3-8B, with this tested roleplay configuration, does not meet the requested reliability for release. No claim that more parameters alone fix these failures. No Android integration or new APK was performed.
